newsitem.title: FRANCE: Prosecutor says bomb hit Juppe's mayoral office.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutor says bomb hit Juppe's mayoral office.

text.p: A public prosecutor said on Sunday that a bomb caused a blast which damaged the mayoral offices of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux in southwestern France overnight.
Public prosecutor Patrice Davost told reporters that explosives caused the blast shortly before midnight (2200 GMT Saturday) at the city hall. It caused no casualties.
Davost said no threats had been received before the powerful device exploded. No one had claimed responsibility.

The centre-right Juppe was absent when the explosion shattered windows in a hall of the elegant building at 11.41 p.m. (2141 GMT). Police said it had probably been caused by a bomb placed at ground level beneath the windows of the ornate reception rooms.

Juppe, who took office as prime minister early last year, regularly visits the port city but he does not reside at the city hall. He had left Bordeaux on Saturday afternoon to return to Paris and was expected to return to Bordeaux on Sunday morning, officials said.
The building was sealed off by police who searched through the upper floors.
